study reveals why mosquitoes bite humans more often have a clear preference new research found that mosquitoes are becoming increasingly attracted to humans and scientists say that we the humans are to blame for this the research published in frontiers in ecology and evolution suggests that human activities like deforestation and climate change are driving this shift in mosquito behaviour scientists conducted a study on mosquitoes in brazil and found that as forests shrink and wildlife populations decline these bloodsucking insects are left with fewer options making humans a convenient alternative

built for real life how a wellinstalled fence transforms outdoor living in east tennessee in east tennessee outdoor spaces arent just for looks theyre meant to be lived in from backyard firepits and patios to family gatherings that stretch late into the evening homeowners need fencing that does more than mark a property line a fence needs to withstand heat rain shifting ground and real everyday use thats where quality fence installation makes the difference east tennessee conditions demand better fence construction knoxville and the surrounding areas experience hot summers heavy rainfall and freezing temperatures in winter these conditions can quickly expose weaknesses in poorly installed fences posts that arent set correctly can shift wood that isnt properly treated or spaced can warp and rot vinyl and chain link can fail early if installed without accounting for terrain and drainage a fence that lasts in east tennessee isnt about cutting corners its about building correctly from the start fencing around firepits retaining walls and outdoor features one of the most overlooked aspects of fence installation is how it integrates with outdoor living features firepits retaining walls patios and elevation changes all require a higher level of planning and precision installing fencing near a retaining wall or firepit means accounting for soil pressure and drainage heat exposure proper post anchoring safety and spacing visual flow of the space when done correctly fencing enhances the atmosphere rather than interrupting it a wellplaced fence can frame a firepit area create privacy and make a backyard feel like an extension of the home not an afterthought fence materials that perform in east tennessee different materials serve different needs but all require proper installation to reach their full lifespan wood fencing remains popular for its natural look but longevity depends on post depth spacing and airflow to prevent moisture damage vinyl fencing offers low maintenance and longterm durability but only when installed on stable footings that prevent movement and cracking chain link fencing is a practical solution for many properties especially on uneven terrain but must be tensioned and set correctly to avoid sagging over time farm and agricultural fencing requires even more attention to ground conditions especially across large or sloped properties common in east tennessee why timing matters building before the spring rush many homeowners assume fence projects should wait until spring in reality winter and earlyyear installations often offer advantages faster scheduling fewer weather delays than expected more flexibility for complex installs your property is ready before peak outdoor season planning ahead allows homeowners to enjoy their outdoor spaces the moment warmer weather arrives not wait in line for availability built to last means installed right a fence isnt just a product its a system posts rails panels hardware and installation methods all work together even premium materials will fail prematurely if installed incorrectly especially in east tennessees demanding climate thats why working with an experienced local fence contractor matters someone who understands soil conditions drainage challenges and how to build fences that last year after year serving knoxville and surrounding areas loudon county fence position in the meta is unique and interesting enough that it deserves more than the summary i initially gave so today im going to do a more indepth reconsideration of the hippopotamus did it really deserve the atier rating or was i lowballing it today were going to find out hippopotamus build analysis hippopotamus build history like the elephant the hippopotamus is something of an anomaly in the current meta with few close relatives among living organisms hippos arose from a group of ungulates called the whippomorphs which diverged from other artiodactyl ungulates the group that includes all hooved mammals with an even number of toes in the midtolate paleocene around 59 million years ago in the early eocene around 54 million years ago whippomorphs themselves underwent a further split into two distinct guilds one group quickly started developing aquatic specialisations to the point that they would eventually give up all terrestrial traits completely and would move from freshwater to the oceans the descendants of these species are known today as cetaceans or more commonly as whales the other group remained for a time as terrestrial herbivores and the descendants of this group would become known as anthracotheres from the start eocene anthracotheres already resembled shrunken hippos in a number of ways though they also retained a number of traits that made them look a little bit like hippopig hybrids however eocene anthracotheres were still predominantly terrestrial animals not yet having adapted to a semiaquatic lifestyle their move to being semiaquatic didnt begin until the oligocene and miocene as shifts in global climates led to a number of anthracotheres environments becoming hotter and more arid at varying times to protect against taking damage from the heat several anthracothere lineages independently started spending more and more time in water and specced into a variety of aquatic adaptations to help facilitate this the first example of this trend occurred with the bothriodontine anthracotheres in the early oligocene whose strategy was then separately copied by a few other lineages in the early miocene one of these early miocene guilds would adapt enough to become a new group called the hippopotamids as the name suggests this is the guild that modernday hippos are part of throughout the late miocene hippopotamids spread and radiated into becoming a successful guild while shifting climates possibly combined with increased hippopotamid competition led to the vast majority of anthracotheres dying out only a few south asian anthracotheres survived and these would go on to die out in the pliocene leaving the few surviving hippopotamid builds as the last remaining hippopotamoids hippopotamids continued to be a relatively diverse and successful group up until the late pleistocene and holocene when the vast majority of them were wiped out by human invasions along with most other megafauna of the era in the end the only two hippopotamoid builds to make it to the present day were two types of hippopotamus the common hippopotamus usually just called the hippopotamus and its smaller relative the pygmy hippopotamus note from here on out unless stated otherwise any references to the hippopotamus will be intended to refer specifically to the common hippopotamus statements meant to include the pygmy hippopotamus andor extinct hippopotamid species will refer to hippopotamids with that out of the way what is it about the hippopotamus thats allowed it to survive and remain dominant after so many of its relatives have died out to find out lets now go into the hippopotamuss stats and abilities hippopotamus stats and abilities aquatic adaptations density when looking at aquatic or semiaquatic mammal builds the first thing that usually needs to be looked at when understanding them is how theyve actually adapted to the water hippos are among the strangest of all mammals in this regard in that theyre the only semiaquatic mammals that have not evolved the ability to swim i dont just mean that they arent specialized for swimming i mean that they cant swim at all even to the extent that most terrestrial mammals can instead the hippopotamus has evolved a body plan with extradense bones making them negatively buoyant when in a river lake or swamp a hippo will naturally sink to the bottom where it can travel using an unusual means of locomotion called underwater punting to punt hippos push off of the river floor with their feet and then glide through the water for an extended period pushing off the floor again to generate thrust when they come back down in this way hippos are able to essentially gallop underwater moving with a grace that would not be possible for a similarlylarge animal on land this isnt quite the same as the more wellknown galloping of horses though when terrestrial animals gallop the gait they form is an unstable one on land and they have to compensate by increasing their speed to maintain a dynamic equilibrium hippos have it a little easier because their galloping gait is partly supported by the buoyancy of the water around them while they can do it quickly its not a requirement in this way being a hippo underwater is a little bit like walking in zero gravity other aquatic adaptations like most animals that live in water hippos dont need to put as many points into supporting their own weight as a terrestrial animal of equivalent size would this is why their legs are proportionally shorter than those of other comparable african megafauna like elephants or giraffes also like many semiaquatic animals hippos have their eyes ears and nose on top of the head allowing them to keep track of things above the water while still remaining mostly submerged combat the hippopotamus as the third largest land animal in the current meta after the elephant and rhinoceros this is sortof true but slightly misleading in that putting them behind rhinos is somewhat understating just how huge hippos can get the maximum weight of any animal is often difficult to determine but credible sources put the masses of the largest hippos at around 3200 kg which is actually larger than most living rhinoceroses are known to get only the white rhinoceros is known to grow to even larger sizes even if you focus on averages instead of maxima the average hippopotamus weighs roughly 1500 kg thats still larger than the average weights for three of the five living rhinoceros species surpassed only by the white and indian rhinoceroses so if you are going to lump all five rhinoceros species together into one type of animal its arguably more accurate to say that hippos and rhinos are tied for the second most massive living land animal rather than saying that hippos rank third either way hippos are the largest living members of the artiodactyl faction and their sheer mass is enough by itself to make almost any predator think twice about attacking one bite one thing that stands out about hippos when compared to other large herbivores is that they rely on a somewhat unusual defensive strategy in the current meta most large herbivores rely on weapons like horns antlers or tusks for defence but the hippo is perhaps the only nonpredator whose main defensive weapon is its jaw female hippos have been found in field tests to bite with up to 1800 pounds of force or around 8000 newtons given that the males have larger jaws a bull hippo would presumably be able to bite with even greater force but no dataminer has yet been brave enough to take a precise measurement nevertheless even the females bite completely blows any other living herbivore out of the water as well as every land predator in the current meta among all extant animals only crocodilians and some large sharks are known to be able to bite harder as ive noted before though bite force by itself is often overrated as a metric for damagedealing capacity in the case of hippos what really makes them so dangerous is the combination of their overpowered bite force with their absurdly wide gape hippos have the largest mouths of any land animal in the current meta and their jaws hinge is so far back that they can open their mouth to a nearly 150degree angle achieving this kind of gape might well tear the muscles of another mammal but hippos jaws have undergone extensive modifications not seen in other mammals which enable them to handle it safely a hippos mouth is so big that a fullgrown lionesss entire head can fit inside it meaning that a hippos jaw has both enough space and enough force to crush most predators skulls in one attack thick skin despite what you might assume from their chubby appearance very little of a hippos body weight comes from fat instead their shape comes from having an enormous amount of muscle guarded by an exceptionally thick layer of skin hippos skin can be as much as 35 centimetres in thickness which is more than 17 times as thick as typical human skin and is unusual even for such a massive animal combined with their sheer size this is more than enough to make fullgrown hippos virtually immune to attacks from predators there have been documented instances where groups of lions have attempted to gang up on adult hippopotamuses only to find that the hippopotamus can simply ignore their attacks i dont mean that the hippos will shrug off the attack and then run away or even that theyll retaliate i mean theyll literally just ignore the attacks and continue walking around with multiple lions clawing onto their backs as if they dont even notice anything unusual nonhuman predators are just that little threat to them in theory a hippos armour could likely still be penetrated by some of the other megafaunal weapons of the african savanna such as the elephants tusks or the rhinoceross horns however its not very common for an elephant or rhinoceros to have any reason to attack a hippopotamus so this only rarely comes up in nature other than humans the only animals that are likely to pose a danger to hippopotamuses under normal circumstances are other hippopotamuses blood sweat moving outside of pvp to defence against environmental hazards another useful defensive ability hippos have is that they can secrete a viscous fluid from their skin when in the sun which acts as a protective coating this fluid is often called blood sweat although this is misleading as it contains no blood and is also not actually sweat rather the socalled sweat consists of two acidic pigments called hipposudoric acid and norhipposudoric acid though initially colourless the mixture quickly turns red after being secreted which is the reason for the blood part of the name these pigments offer added protection for hippos in two main ways firstly both of these pigments have an absorption spectrum that allows them to easily absorb the ultraviolet light from the hot african sun effectively acting as a kind of allnatural sunblock second both pigments also have some antibiotic properties and can be used to inhibit the growth of certain harmful bacteria feeding eating grasses one big thing that separates hippos from most aquatic or semiaquatic mammals is the fact that theyre herbivores rivers and lakes can be difficult environments for large herbivores to adapt to as plants generally have more difficulty growing in flowing water than they do on land hippos deal with this problem by not relying on the water for food very much if at all instead hippos spend most of the daytime in the water to keep cool and then come onto land to feed on terrestrial plants at night nearly all of a hippos diet comes from terrestrial grasses with only minimal consumption of underwater plants digestion a hippopotamuss digestive system is unusual for a large herbivore in several ways among living herbivorous megafauna almost all of them take one of two approaches when it comes to digestion on the one hand there are herbivores that chew their cud like cattle antelope and giraffes also known as ruminants cudchewing herbivores have stomachs that are divided into multiple chambers and will regurgitate their food several times during the digestive process so that it can rechew whats left of them to break them down further before theyre sent to the next chamber this strategy is optimized for getting the maximum nutrition out of each individual bit of food on the other hand you have hindgut fermenters like horses elephants and rhinoceroses as ive discussed in the past these animals dont primarily rely on their stomachs for digestion instead using their stomach to store food until it can be passed to the large intestine where the symbiotic bacteria handle the real work as ive also noted before this strategy is designed to maximize the sheer volume of food that an animal can take in and process in a given feeding period which is why it tends to be favoured by the very largest of the megafauna the hippopotamus is unique among living herbivorous megafauna in that it doesnt use either of these strategies while their stomach is divided into three chambers hippopotamuses are not true ruminants and they do not have access to the chew cud ability in fact hippos can barely chew their food at all in their drive to turn their mouths into the ultimate death machines theyve evolved such massive incisors that they block the jaws from being able to move from sidetoside when feeding resulting in the single least effective chewing motion seen in any herbivorous mammal to compensate for this hippopotamuses have evolved to digest food more slowly than most ruminants giving their stomachs extra time to break down what their mouths cant however since they still do most of their digestion in the stomach they dont have a place where they can just keep huge amounts of food for later processing once space opens up the way hindgut fermenters do consequently hippos are stuck in a kind of worstofbothworlds scenario from a feeding standpoint not getting as much value out of each food item as ruminants but also not able to handle as large a quantity of food as hindgut fermenters this isnt necessarily a major problem provided that they live in an environment with enough highquality feed but its not surprising that successful large herbivores so rarely go for this strategy overall hippo tier rating on the whole i think my original tier ranking for the hippopotamus holds up well in the right environment one where they have easy access to large amounts of shallow water during the day and to lots of highquality plant food at night their nearlyunparalleled combat kit makes them one of the best herbivore picks that you can find other than humans they have very little to fear from any predator or from almost any other build in general but i still think its kind of a silly choice to spend so many of your points adapting to shallow water and then put barely any points into either swimming or underwater feeding and for an animal thats so massive and therefore requires a huge amount of food to survive the limitations of the hippos digestive system cannot be overlooked compared to the servers other gigantic tanks hippos dont have any flaws that are as crippling as rhinoceroses propensity for killing each other in combat but theyre a little too minimaxed to be as overwhelmingly dominant as the elephant putting hippos in a tier right inbetween where i placed the other two still seems fair so thats my analysis of the hippopotamus i hope you enjoyed it why the term fossil fuel is being questioned a recent debate has begun over whether the world should rethink the term fossil fuel the discussion gained attention after a senior leader of a major oil producers group argued that the phrase is scientifically imprecise and shapes public perception in a misleading way his comments have sparked responses from economists energy analysts and experts around the world highlighting how language influences climate conversations and energy policy why the term is being challenged the main argument is that the word fuel does not fully describe how crude oil is actually used crude oil is rarely burned in its raw form instead it is refined into thousands of products some used as fuel but many others used in everyday life plastics medicines chemicals cosmetics fertilizers and countless industrial materials come from oilderived substances according to industry projections the petrochemical sector is expected to be the single largest driver of additional oil demand between 2024 and 2050 this means oils future relevance may be tied more to nonfuel products not just gasoline or diesel another point raised is the word fossil fossilization is a process where organic matter turns into solid rock over millions of years by contrast oil forms when organic material is heated and transformed deep underground a different geological process some argue that if global climate debates insist on scientific accuracy then using a broad nonscientific term for oil may not be appropriate what supporters of the term say those who oppose changing the terminology say the problem is not the origin of the word but the carbon emissions associated with oil coal and gas in their view whether or not the term is perfect it effectively signals that these energy sources release carbon that was locked underground for millions of years some analysts also pointed out that the proposed alternatives were never clearly stated without a new name a call for change may only cause confusion others noted that focusing too much on terminology could distract from the real challenge reducing emissions some experts added that the distinction between energy use and nonenergy use of oil is important but still doesnt remove the need to consider carbon footprints why some believe this is about narrative not science several energy market observers believe the call for renaming oil is part of an effort to reshape global conversations as the world discusses energy transition some countries and producers prefer the phrase energy addition suggesting that new technologies should grow alongside oil and gas rather than replace them they argue that changing labels wont change the core debate which is about how quickly and how deeply countries cut emissions what global politics has to do with it political leaders in some major oilproducing countries have strong reasons to preserve the role of oil in the world economy meanwhile in the united states policies under the current administration are geared towards supporting domestic oil and petrochemical industries through deregulation and incentives this adds to the complexity of how different nations frame discussions about the future of oil where the conversation goes from here the push to reconsider the term fossil fuel is not expected to bring immediate changes but it does show how strongly language can influence public debate climate narratives and policy decisions as governments companies and climate groups continue to negotiate the future of energy the words used to describe different energy sources may become more important than ever in the end whether or not the name changes the global challenge remains the same how to balance energy needs economic growth and environmental responsibility in a world facing rapid climate change

transform your durban home aesthetics with smart lighting solutions smart lighting often gets talked about as a cool gadget upgrade but its much more useful to think of it as a way to shape how your home feels and functions throughout the day when the technology fades into the background and simply supports how you live that is when it is doing its job well a helpful starting point is to stop thinking about lights as only on or off and instead think about them in terms of layers and behaviour layers are about where the light comes from and what it does general lighting to see the room task lighting to work or read and accent lighting to highlight features or create mood behaviour is about how that light changes the colour temperature brightness timing and whether it reacts to you or follows a schedule smart lighting gives you control over both layers and behaviour with much more precision than a conventional setup colour temperature is one of the most powerful tools cooler white light higher kelvin values feels crisp and energising while warmer white light lower kelvin values feels calm and intimate in a coastal or warm humid climate many people prefer a slightly cooler white during the day to balance the natural warmth in their environment but still want a very warm soft tone at night with tunable smart lamps or downlights you can set your daytime scenes to a neutral or cool white that keeps spaces feeling bright and clean then automatically shift to warm white in the evening over time these subtle transitions support your natural circadian rhythm and can make your home feel more restful without you needing to constantly adjust switches brightness and contrast matter just as much as colour a common mistake is relying heavily on a single bright ceiling light in each room this often makes a space feel flat or even harsh especially if you live in a place with strong natural daylight during part of the day and very dark evenings smart dimming allows you to match the intensity of your artificial light to the ambient conditions for example in the late afternoon you might only need a soft fill from wall lights or floor lamps while the sun is still present after dark you can bring up your general lighting slightly but keep accent lights focused on artwork plants or textured walls to maintain depth and interest automations and scenes are where the system becomes genuinely helpful rather than just novel instead of thinking of movie mode or party mode first it is often more valuable to design a handful of everyday scenes a morning scene that gradually brightens over 1020 minutes using cooler clearer light in kitchens and bathrooms to help you wake up a work or focus scene in your study or dining area that increases task lighting on desks and benches while keeping background lighting softer so screens are more comfortable to view an evening winddown scene that shifts the entire home toward warmer tones and lower brightness levels particularly in bedrooms and living rooms a night path that uses very lowlevel warm light in passages and bathrooms so navigating at night does not disturb sleep motion sensors contact sensors and smart switches can support these scenes without requiring you to interact with an app every time for example a sensor in a hallway might trigger lowlevel warm lighting after sunset but stay off during the day when natural light is sufficient practical considerations are important too reliable connectivity and a clear plan for which lights are smart and which remain conventional will make the system easier to live with many people overcomplicate things by trying to make every single fitting smart in reality choosing key zones for smart control is often more effective main living areas circulation spaces exterior entrances and bedrooms typically provide the most benefit compatibility with existing wiring and fittings is another factor sometimes it is simpler to keep your existing luminaires and use smart lamps other times especially in ceilings with downlights swapping to dedicated smart fixtures or using smart switches is the cleaner more robust option an experienced lighting team like future light will usually begin by mapping how each room is used what natural light it receives and how the current wiring is laid out before suggesting which approach makes sense it is also worth considering how guests or less techcomfortable family members will interact with your lighting keeping key wall switches operational even if they control smart circuits can avoid frustration many ecosystems now support smart wall controls that look and behave like normal switches but trigger scenes or dimming behind the scenes finally remember that smart lighting is not just functional it can subtly highlight the character of your home in a region with strong sun outdoor and patio lighting can be set to come on gradually at dusk with very warm tones that complement natural materials and planting gentle accent lighting on architectural details water features or textured walls can make outdoor spaces feel inviting without excessive brightness or glare used thoughtfully smart lighting is less about gadgets and more about comfort rhythm and atmosphere if you approach it by asking how you want each space to feel at different times of day and then use technology to support those answers you are far more likely to end up with a system that feels natural and quietly effective over the long term

cloudy with a chance of conspiracy the wild world of chemtrails vs contrails i was lying on my back in the grass last tuesday watching a jet etch its white line across the blue when my neighbor leaned over the fence theyre at it again he said shaking his head who them spraying us i blinked the contrail was already dissolving into wisps this is how it starts not with dramatic music or a smoking gun but with a simple question what are those lines in the sky and depending on who you ask youll get two very different answers the science whats actually happening up there when a plane flies at high altitude were talking 30000 feet and above its engines burn fuel and spit out hot humid exhaust the air up there is cold really cold often colder than 40f what happens next is basic physics water vapor from the exhaust hits that frigid air and instantly condenses into tiny ice crystals those crystals catch the light thats your contrail short for condensation trail sometimes they vanish in seconds other times if the air is humid enough they stick around and spread into cirruslike clouds the atmospheric conditions determine how long they last not whats in them meteorologists have been documenting this since the 1920s back when highaltitude flight was still new and strange its the same principle that lets you see your breath on a winter morning just happening six miles up the conspiracy enter the chemtrail but for a growing number of people those lines arent innocent byproducts of combustion theyre evidence of something darker the chemtrail theory suggests that certain aircraft are deliberately releasing chemical or biological agents into the atmosphere for weather modification population control psychological manipulation or some combination thereof the trails that linger too long spread too wide form grid patterns in the sky those arent contrails those are chemtrails ive gone down this rabbit hole more than once late at night with too much coffee the forums the youtube documentaries with ominous music the analysis of unusual flight patterns theres a whole ecosystem of people photographing skies testing rainwater connecting dots and i get it i really do why this one sticks most conspiracy theories ask you to believe in hidden agendas this one asks you to believe your own eyes look up there they are white lines crisscrossing the sky sometimes dozens of them if youve never thought about it before it does look weird it does look like somethings being sprayed and once you start noticing you cant stop the chemtrail narrative offers something seductive an explanation for the vague unease many of us feel about the world why does everything feel off why do so many people seem sick anxious exhausted maybe its not capitalism or climate change or the slow grind of modern life maybe its the sky its a story that makes the invisible visible it names the enemy and in a world that often feels impossibly complex and out of our control that clarity even if its false clarity can feel like relief the gap between feeling and fact heres where i land and its not a place of smug certainty the scientific consensus is overwhelming atmospheric scientists chemists meteorologists people whove spent their entire careers studying air and weather all say the same thing those are contrails ice crystals not chemicals independent researchers have tested the air the water the soil no secret spraying programs have been verified commercial pilots military pilots aviation engineers thousands of people who would have to be in on it have spoken up to say this isnt happening but feelings dont care about consensus if you feel unsafe if you feel manipulated if you look at the institutions that are supposed to protect you and see corruption or indifference then why would you trust them about this why would you believe the experts when experts have been wrong before when theyve lied before when they serve power before people thats the real conversation here not the science the trust what i think about when i look up i believe there are experiments and ongoing cloud seeding projects but i dont believe in wholesale chemical warfare its easy to track the cause of a trail by going to flightradar24com i believe in the instinct that makes people look up and question what theyre being told i think we live in a time when its rational to be suspicious when corporations do poison communities and cover it up when governments have conducted secret experiments on their own citizens when the truth has been bent so many times that skepticism feels like survival the tragedy is when that healthy skepticism gets misdirected when were so busy staring at contrails that we miss the actual pollution the stuff we know is killing us the carbon the plastics the forever chemicals in our water the air quality alerts that are becoming routine those things dont require a conspiracy theyre happening in broad daylight with paperwork living in the question im not here to convince anyone if you believe in chemtrails nothing i say will change your mind and honestly thats okay were all trying to make sense of a world that often doesnt make sense what i will say is this the sky is big enough for uncertainty you can look up and wonder you can notice the planes the patterns the way some days the trails linger and some days they dont you can ask questions you can be curious about what youre breathing whats being done to the planet who benefits and who pays just maybe also leave room for the mundane answer sometimes a contrail is just ice crystals catching light sometimes the conspiracy is quieter and closer than we think not in the sky but in the soil the water the policies written in fine print sometimes the hardest truth is that there isnt a single villain to unmask just a thousand small violences weve all agreed to live with i still lie in the grass and watch the planes i still see the white lines i still wonder about the world and what were doing to it but mostly im just here present breathing watching the sky do what it does and that i think is its own kind of power
